study.title: A Patient-Specific Registration of Coronary Angiogram-Fluoroscopy by Similarity-Based Transfer Learning

imaging.modality_detail: Diagnostic coronary X-ray angiography cine loop registered to live X-ray fluoroscopy during PCI (dynamic coronary roadmapping)
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries during percutaneous coronary intervention
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 15 (standardized; sequences of approximately 15 to 30 frames covering at least one cardiac cycle)

annotation.annotator_expertise: experts (virtual guidewires along manually labeled vessel centerlines)

task.task_description: Patient-specific deep-learning registration of a diagnostic coronary angiogram sequence to live fluoroscopy (guidewire overlay) without ECG gating, using a Res-U-Net image generator and fast transfer learning from the most similar pre-trained model selected via PCA and cosine similarity within the same C-arm configuration class.
task.clinical_application: Dynamic coronary roadmapping for guidewire navigation during percutaneous coronary intervention, including patients with arrhythmia

temporal_evidence.quote: optimized to generate **predicted** registered images by taking m-step **virtual** guidewire images stacked with an angiographic sequence from the new patient’s angiogram

method.pretraining: Transfer learning from patient-specific Res-U-Net models pre-trained offline on previous patients; the most similar model is selected by PCA/cosine similarity within the same C-arm configuration class

metrics.metric: Transfer learning time with most similar pre-trained model to reach t-PSNR 30 dB
Transfer learning epochs with most similar pre-trained model
Res-U-Net scratch training time to reach v-PSNR > 33 dB
Transfer learning time reduction vs all other pre-trained models

comparators: Transfer learning with all other pre-trained models
Generalized transfer learning (single model pre-trained on 51 datasets)

G1.quote: The number of datasets for certain C-arm angles was small.

G2.quote: more diverse and comprehensive clinical dataset is necessary in future to validate the proposed approach

G4.quote: The use of two-dimensional data may not capture the full complexity that three-dimensional data offer for clinical scenarios.

G5.quote: they generally require many patient datasets, which is a major problem. Therefore, a data-efficient approach is required for both practical and economic reasons.

G6.quote: Future clinical trials are essential to comprehensively validate the effectiveness and safety of the model in real-world conditions.

G9.quote: even in rare conditions, such as anomalies occurring in less than 1 % of cases

other_limitations: Suboptimal angiogram quality (blur, patient movement) hinders learning
Severely blocked vessels give partial angiographic views, hampering alignment
Guidewire tip bending/deformation not specifically addressed
Most similar pre-trained model does not always give the fastest transfer learning
future_work: Collect more diverse and comprehensive clinical datasets including rare anatomical anomalies
Clinical trials to validate effectiveness and safety in real-world conditions
More datasets per C-arm angle to improve pre-trained model selection
Refine model for robustness and reliability in clinical settings
